name: hoard

attributes.attribute: Celtic treasures hidden in bogs and similar places
includes gold torcs, decorated cauldrons, and lunae or moon-collars
one purpose of hoards, possibly during epidemics or disasters

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A hoard is an archaeological site. Celtic hoards rest in bogs and similar hiding places. They hold gold torcs, decorated cauldrons, and lunae or moon-collars. Scholars believe people hid the treasures in bogs to protect them from invaders, perhaps Vikings. People also deposited hoards as sacrifice, possibly during epidemics or other threatened or actual disasters.

okr.objective: Document the Celtic hoard as an archaeological site.
key_results: Record why scholars believe treasures were hidden in bogs.
Note the use of hoards as sacrifice during disasters.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): hoard entry.
